statements.text: Every task representation carries an integer `version`, serialized as `version`.
`POST /tasks` returns HTTP 201 with a task whose `version` is 1.
Tasks seeded into the store at startup start at `version` 1.
Every successful `PUT /tasks/{id}` increments the task's `version` by exactly 1 (1 -> 2 -> 3 ...).
`UpdateTaskRequest` accepts an optional integer field `expectedVersion`; omitting it is valid.
When `expectedVersion` is omitted (null), the update proceeds unconditionally (backward-compatible last-writer-wins) and returns HTTP 200 with the version incremented.
When `expectedVersion` is provided and equals the task's current `version`, the update succeeds with HTTP 200 and the version increments.
When `expectedVersion` is provided and does not equal the task's current `version`, the update is rejected with HTTP 409 Conflict.
A rejected (409) update leaves the task entirely unchanged: no field is updated and the version is not bumped.

The version comparison and the version increment are performed atomically inside `TaskStore`, so two concurrent writers cannot both succeed from the same observed version (ADR 2026-08-04-optimistic-concurrency-in-the-store).
The existing PUT integration test, which omits `expectedVersion`, keeps passing unchanged; `dotnet build` and `dotnet test` stay green (R-003).
`GET /tasks`, `GET /tasks/{id}`, `DELETE /tasks/{id}`, the blank-title 400 validation, and the 404-on-unknown-id behaviour of PUT are unchanged.
The domain layer gains no dependency on the HTTP layer (R-004) and `TaskState` naming is preserved (R-005).
